meanings.en: in my opinion, to my mind
meanings.note: Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem '-моему').

examples.trans: In my opinion, not bad. It fits great!
In my opinion, this is disgusting!
I think he's right.

meanings.note: Negative prefix 'не-' ('un-, non-, not') (stem 'плохо'). Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.trans: In my opinion, not bad. It fits great!
Well then, not bad.
He speaks Russian pretty well.

meanings.note: Prefix 'от-' ('away from, off') marks separation, completion, or response (stem 'лично'). Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.trans: In my opinion, not bad. It fits great!
I know this town really well!
Everything went great.

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'идеть'). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'is sitting', paired with 'посидеть'.

examples.trans: Why are you sitting in the corner?
I'm sitting in a café.
Never been in prison?

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'пасибо'). Common neuter noun meaning 'thank you' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Нет, спасибо. Я сегодня на диете.
examples.trans: No, thank you. I am on a diet today.

examples.text: Спасибо, Соломон Иванович. Теперь всё можно!
examples.trans: Thank you, Solomon Ivanovich. Now everything is allowed!
Thanks, Dad!

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian conversational adverb meaning 'now', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Спасибо, Соломон Иванович. Теперь всё можно!
examples.trans: Thank you, Solomon Ivanovich. Now everything is allowed!
Now I'm the boss.
Now everything's fine.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'everything', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Заодно объясню, почему всё так вышло.
examples.trans: At the same time I will explain why it all happened this way.
Forgive me, I mixed everything up.

examples.text: Спасибо, Соломон Иванович. Теперь всё можно!
examples.trans: Thank you, Solomon Ivanovich. Now everything is allowed!

meanings.note: Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.text: Может, это она на вас так влияет?
examples.trans: Maybe she is influencing you like that?
Maybe she is the one who decided?
Maybe I can pay you extra?

meanings.note: Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('good').

examples.trans: Good news. Gulya agrees.

examples.text: Хорошо. Слушай, ну это деловая встреча.
examples.trans: Alright. Listen, well this is a business meeting.

examples.text: Ты такой хороший. Только не обижайся.
examples.trans: You are so good. Only do not take offense.

meanings.note: Abstract feminine noun formed with the Slavic suffix '-ость' ('-ness, -ity') from the corresponding adjective. Common feminine noun meaning 'news' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: Good news. Gulya agrees.
Good news!
Watch the news.

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'огласный'). Adjective formed with the common Slavic suffix '-н-' from a noun/verb root. Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('agreeable, agree').

examples.trans: Good news. Gulya agrees.
I agree.
I agree to this bet!

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian clause-linking conjunction meaning 'but', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Why do you not wear it?
I am telling you for sure!
What is the matter, Lyova? Easy.

meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'there is'.

examples.trans: I wanted to look like you.
I have a toy car.
Childhood was hard.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian clause-linking conjunction meaning 'and', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Go have breakfast later.
Just as I assumed.
You said it was a crack.

meanings.note: Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('bad').

examples.trans: In my opinion, not bad. It fits great!
But there is also bad news.
Bad weather.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'to you', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: You have to tell me.
Did you chop the carrots?
Why do you not wear it?

meanings.en: to have to, to be forced to
meanings.note: Prefix 'при-' indicates approaching, attachment, or slight degree of action (stem 'йтись'). Reflexive/intransitive verb with the postfix '-ся'/'-сь' (historically from the reflexive pronoun 'себя', oneself). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'it will be necessary', paired with 'приходиться'.

examples.trans: I'm going to have to torture you.
We had to wait a long time.

examples.text: Ты что, очкарик, не понимаешь? Мне тебя мучить придётся.
examples.trans: Don't you get it, four-eyes? I'm going to have to torture you.

meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to wait, to expect', paired with 'подождать'.

examples.trans: You will have to wait a whole week.
Don't wait for me.
I'm waiting for you.

meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'kisses, kiss', paired with 'поцеловать'.

examples.trans: Bye, kisses!
Mum kisses the child.
Well, call me, kitten. Bye, kisses!

meanings.note: Negative prefix 'не-' ('un-, non-, not') (stem 'деля'). Common feminine noun meaning 'week' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: In a week you will recover.
You will have to wait a whole week.

examples.text: Значит, я зря целую неделю мучил себя диетами! Ты просто чудо!
examples.trans: So for a whole week I tormented myself with diets in vain! You are simply a miracle!

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian discourse particle adding conversational nuance meaning 'only', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Only a wardrobe fell.
And I will speak only the truth.
I speak only the truth!

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'she', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Well, that is what it is.
She is my niece.

examples.text: Может, это она на вас так влияет?
examples.trans: Maybe she is influencing you like that?

meanings.note: Prefix 'про-' indicates movement through, completion, or missing the mark (stem 'сить'). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'asked for', paired with 'попросить'.

examples.trans: You asked me yourself, chef.

examples.text: Только она просила никому не говорить.
examples.trans: Only she asked not to tell anyone.

examples.text: И шеф попросил меня сводить тебя в ресторан.
examples.trans: And the chef asked me to take you out to the restaurant.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'anyone', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Did nobody take the truffles?

examples.text: Вы никогда на диету не садились, шеф.
examples.trans: You never went on a diet before, chef.

examples.text: Этого вообще никто не видел. Правда, Макс?
examples.trans: Nobody saw a thing at all. Right, Max?

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian discourse particle adding conversational nuance meaning 'not', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: You have an incomplete rib fracture.
No. Stop it!
And why do I not know?

meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to speak', paired with 'сказать'.

examples.trans: And I will speak only the truth.

examples.text: Только она просила никому не говорить.
examples.trans: Only she asked not to tell anyone.
That's what you said.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian conversational adverb meaning 'very', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: And why do I not know?

examples.text: Если хочешь её удивить, скажи что-нибудь.
examples.trans: If you want to surprise her, say something.

examples.text: Вот что ты ей хочешь сказать?
examples.trans: Now what do you want to say to her?

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'трогий'). Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('strict').

examples.trans: Ainura is very strict, she might forbid it.
How strict you are, Klavdia Viktorovna.

examples.text: У нас в школе очень строгий директор.
examples.trans: We have a very strict principal at our school.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian conversational adverb meaning 'maybe', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Может, это она на вас так влияет?
examples.trans: Maybe she is influencing you like that?
Maybe she is the one who decided?
Maybe I can pay you extra?

meanings.note: Prefix 'за-' marks beginning an action, covering, or stopping by along the way (stem 'претить'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to forbid', paired with 'запрещать'.

examples.trans: Ainura is very strict, she might forbid it.
But Anikeev forbade it!
The doctor forbade him to drink.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'you (polite/plural)', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: You said it was a crack.

examples.text: Вы же знаете, кто у вас будет?
examples.trans: Do you know who you are having?
She is working her first day today.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian spatial or relational preposition meaning 'on, onto', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: You said it was a crack.
Well, that is what it is.
Be glad. How was the injury sustained?

meanings.note: Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'хожий'). Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('similar, look like').

examples.trans: You look like Iosif Prigozhin.
Well done, he looks like him! Congratulations.
Then he would have looked completely alike.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian spatial or relational preposition meaning 'to, towards', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Go have breakfast later.
Just as I assumed.
You said it was a crack.

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'ожаление'). Verbal action/result neuter noun formed with '-ение'/'-ание'. Common neuter noun meaning 'regret (unfortunately)' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: К сожалению, я он и есть.
examples.trans: Unfortunately, I am him.
Unfortunately, I'm busy.

examples.text: Вы, к сожалению, не в моём вкусе.
examples.trans: Unfortunately, you are not my type.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'I', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Just as I assumed.
And why do I not know?
I do not owe you anything.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'he', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Well, that is what it is.
She is my niece.
And it will be a bit too big on me!

meanings.en: to knock down, to hit, to strike
meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'бить'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'knocked down, hit', paired with 'сбивать'.

examples.trans: Iosif Prigozhin hit me!

examples.text: Когда я перебегал дорогу, меня сбил Иосиф Пригожин.
examples.trans: When I was running across the road, Iosif Prigozhin hit me.
The driver knocked down a road sign.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian clause-linking conjunction meaning 'if', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Если хочешь её удивить, скажи что-нибудь.
examples.trans: If you want to surprise her, say something.

examples.text: Если можно, пусть это останется между нами.
examples.trans: If possible, let this stay between us.
Come if you want.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian discourse particle adding conversational nuance meaning 'let (them)', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Если можно, пусть это останется между нами.
examples.trans: If possible, let this stay between us.
Let it stay between us!

examples.text: А вот пусть Иосиф Пригожин приедет и расскажет.
examples.trans: Well let Iosif Prigozhin come here and tell it.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'this, it (is)', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Well, that is what it is.
It is just a crack!

examples.text: Я изменился, я сейчас это докажу.
examples.trans: I have changed, I will prove it right now.

meanings.note: Reflexive/intransitive verb with the postfix '-ся'/'-сь' (historically from the reflexive pronoun 'себя', oneself). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'remains', paired with 'оставаться'.

examples.trans: There's nothing left.
I'll stay at home.

examples.text: Ну что, очкарик? Видишь, ничего не осталось.
examples.trans: Well, four-eyes? See, there's nothing left.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian spatial or relational preposition meaning 'between', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Если можно, пусть это останется между нами.
examples.trans: If possible, let this stay between us.
Let it stay between us!
For your information, I am the chairman of the court.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'us', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Кстати, давай мы будем это всё фиксировать.
examples.trans: By the way, let us record all of this.

examples.text: Знаешь, я очень рада, что мы вместе.
examples.trans: You know, I am very glad that we are together.
What do you mean?

meanings.note: Common masculine noun meaning 'darn, heck' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: Damn, Vika!
Darn, I forgot the keys!

examples.text: Чёрт, я запутался. Это опасная идея.
examples.trans: Darn, I am confused. This is a dangerous idea.
